objectives.title: Search Twilio's API instead of guessing
objectives.why: Twilio's API surface spans messaging, voice, verify, email and more — searching for the operation that fits your intent beats recalling an endpoint that may have changed.

objectives.title: Retrieve the full schema before writing a call
objectives.why: Retrieve gives the exact parameters and response shape for an operation, so the code you write matches the real API rather than a remembered one.

objectives.title: Set up your Twilio account and credentials
objectives.why: First-time setup — account, auth and a sender — is the step every other Twilio product depends on, and the easiest one to get subtly wrong.

objectives.title: Plan the use case before picking a product
objectives.why: Twilio has several products that overlap — SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, Verify, Conversations — and an advisor skill helps you choose the right one before code is written.

objectives.title: Send a message
objectives.why: Sending an SMS, WhatsApp or RCS message is the core Twilio loop — the product skill covers the patterns and edge cases the quickstart skips.

objectives.title: Verify a user with a one-time passcode
objectives.why: Verify handles code generation, delivery, rate limiting and fraud checks — rolling your own OTP flow misses most of that.

objectives.title: Build a voice call or TwiML flow
objectives.why: Voice has its own model — TwiML, outbound calls, ConversationRelay for AI agents — and a skill steers you to the right one.

objectives.title: Send email with SendGrid
objectives.why: Email deliverability is its own discipline — the SendGrid skills cover authentication, settings and sending correctly.

objectives.title: Handle webhooks correctly
objectives.why: Inbound messages, status callbacks and events all arrive as webhooks — signature validation and idempotency are what keep them trustworthy.

objectives.title: Orchestrate conversations, flows or routing
objectives.why: Studio, TaskRouter and Conversations let you build workflows on Twilio's side rather than reimplementing them in your own code.

objectives.title: Build an AI agent on Twilio
objectives.why: Twilio's agent skills cover architecture, memory, knowledge and connecting an agent to voice and messaging channels.

objectives.title: Look up phone number intelligence
objectives.why: Validating a number and its line type before sending avoids wasted sends and failed delivery.

objectives.title: Debug with observability tooling
objectives.why: When a message or call fails, the debugger and error codes explain why — far faster than guessing from silence.

bestPractices.title: Harden your integration's security
bestPractices.why: Credentials in source, unvalidated webhooks and over-privileged keys are the common ways a Twilio account gets abused — the security skills cover each.

bestPractices.title: Use API keys, not your Auth Token
bestPractices.why: Twilio recommends API keys for application code — they can be scoped and revoked individually, whereas the Auth Token is the master credential for the whole account.

bestPractices.title: Build in retries, idempotency and status tracking
bestPractices.why: Networks fail and callbacks arrive twice — reliability patterns are what separate a demo from something you can leave running.

bestPractices.title: Check messaging compliance before you send at volume
bestPractices.why: Carriers block unregistered traffic — A2P 10DLC, toll-free verification and opt-out handling need to be in place before launch, not after messages are filtered.

bestPractices.title: Retrieve the schema, then write the call
bestPractices.why: Searching and then retrieving the operation's schema is the intended two-step flow; skipping retrieve is how a plausible-looking parameter turns out not to exist.
